claims: GMB describes a rear-facing palms-up position with fingers toward the knees, a backward shift toward the heels, and a forward return.
Model observable bilateral dorsal-hand contact and increasing/decreasing wrist flexion; do not relabel wrist-flexion bias as proof that one muscle group is isolated or universally stretched.
USA Gymnastics separately identifies a kneeling back-of-hand backward rock as a weight-bearing wrist-flexion exercise but provides no Vortex difficulty score.
Exercise complexity 26, physical difficulty 18, and derived overall 26 are review-only task proposals and never classify a participant.
Gymnastics wrist angles and moments change with hand-support conditions, but back-handspring findings cannot be converted into force values for a lightly loaded dorsal-hand quadruped rocker.

Track complete cycles, wrist-flexion and dorsal-hand support seconds, contact pressure tolerance, support faults, symptoms, and overlapping same-session wrist work; recovery remains a planning estimate.

The review reports substantial wrist-pain and injury burden in adolescent gymnastics with low-to-very-low certainty for available risk-factor evidence; it does not create an age rule or authorize exercise through symptoms.

Selection requires tolerable floor transfer and bilateral dorsal-hand support, comfortable wrist flexion, a clean firm nonabrasive nonslip surface, communication, symptom monitoring, and compatible same-session wrist exposure.
USA Gymnastics says to seek medical guidance when pain is present, discontinue exercises that cause pain, and reduce load or repetitions when form breaks down.

Stop for pain, neurologic or circulation symptoms, dizziness, worsening discomfort, dorsal-hand or finger contact loss, forced range, elbow or shoulder collapse, unsafe surface, or participant request.
GMB presents this as one optional wrist-strengthening/mobility routine element and explicitly says the position can be uncomfortable and must stay within comfortable range.
Use low-volume quality-first Prepare & Access or Movement Intelligence profiles and recompute wrist-flexion, dorsal-hand support, technical-fatigue, duration, and downstream hand-support budgets.
GMB gives a concise fingers-toward-knees, palms-up, back-toward-heels then forward sequence and explicitly prohibits moving into pain.
Athlete support must show backs of hands down, palms up, fingers toward knees, one complete backward-and-forward count, very light comfortable pressure, and a clear stop/help signal.
The USA Gymnastics table supplies a short written back-of-hand backward-rock sequence that can be paired with setup and endpoint images.

Provide front and side demonstrations, a two-frame backward/forward count, slower pace, fewer repetitions, more rest, optional stable knee cushioning, and a separately authored task when dorsal-hand floor contact does not fit.
Five palms-up, rear-facing, or wrist-rock candidates returned current YouTube oEmbed title, channel, thumbnail, and iframe metadata on 2026-08-09.

oEmbed health does not prove playback, exact dorsal-hand/fingers-toward-knees setup, backward-forward repetition, captions, accessibility, cue quality, safety, conflicts, reviewer identity, card-version match, or approval; all remain candidates.

assessmentSummary.identity: A dynamic bilateral quadruped wrist-flexion-biased rocker. Start on hands and knees with the backs of both hands supported, palms facing up, fingers spread comfortably and pointing toward the knees, elbows extended without forced lockout, and pressure initially light. Shift the hips and center of mass backward toward the heels under control only to a comfortable wrist-flexion and dorsal-hand-loading endpoint, then return forward to the declared starting load. One complete backward-and-forward cycle is one repetition. Backward range, tempo, brief comfortable endpoint pause, repetitions, sets, rest, and optional knee cushioning are delivery annotations. Palms down, fingers facing forward or sideways, unilateral loading, circles, palm or finger lifts, sustained holds, tall-plank loading, raised support, bands, manual force, or clinical assessment changes the task.
currentCardFindings: Source 31 has one skeletal baseline variant and generic profile with empty controlled taxonomy, anatomy, load, fatigue, constraints, support, research, alternate, calibration, and exact media review data.
The legacy title says flexor bias, but the observable action is wrist-flexion bias with dorsal-hand support; it does not establish isolated wrist-flexor tissue targeting.
Legacy age, publication, linked-skill, broad outcome, and reviewed-media implications are unsupported and must be cleared or quarantined.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when exact backs-of-hands-down, palms-up, fingers-toward-knees floor support, comfortable wrist-flexion range, elbow/shoulder support, clean firm surface, low dose, duration, symptoms, and downstream wrist budgets fit. Do not convert wrist-flexion bias into a muscle-isolation claim, force range, rotate the hands, add a hold, move to tall plank, or treat the drill as clearance. Choose a separately authored palms-down, palm-lift, isometric, orientation-shift, raised-support, or clinical card when that changed task is intended.

calibrationEvidence.basis: GMB and USA Gymnastics direct exercise descriptions, peer-reviewed gymnastics wrist biomechanics and injury synthesis, current oEmbed metadata, and comparison with neighboring Vortex wrist cards
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source validates one universal hand width, finger spread, wrist angle, backward range, dorsal-hand pressure, pause, dose, frequency, recovery interval, tissue-specific effect, treatment/prevention benefit, eligibility rule, progression order, or Vortex score. Existing media has not been watched in full.

claims: GMB distinguishes rear-facing palms-down and rear-facing palms-up tasks and gives the palms-up task its own setup and comfort warning.
Source 31 therefore remains one backs-of-hands-down, palms-up, fingers-toward-knees dynamic backward-and-forward identity; hand surface and action are not silent annotations.
The task combines a braced quadruped base with controlled upper-extremity support and a sagittal backward/forward weight shift.
Use controlled brace and push patterns; mobility and preparation are contextual purposes rather than invented movement-pattern keys.
Wrist angle and moment vary with gymnastics hand-support conditions, demonstrating that surface and orientation details matter.
The study examines back handsprings, not this rocker, so the card records observable position, contacts, range, exposure time, and symptoms without importing force values.
USA Gymnastics provides a hold-based example and advises fewer repetitions when form fails; it does not validate the Vortex dynamic dose.
Use a conservative review-only range of one to two sets and three to six complete cycles, calculate actual support time, and stop before contact, range, support, or symptom quality degrades.
GMB supports fingers toward the knees, palms up, a backward shift toward the heels, a forward return, slow progression, comfortable range, and no pain.
The card adds exact dorsal-hand contact, complete-cycle counting, light pressure, no bounce, clean stable surface, symptom stops, and actual-dose recording.
The systematic review supports taking gymnastics wrist symptoms and accumulated exposure seriously while emphasizing low certainty and absent training thresholds.

Coach support verifies identity, floor entry, dorsal-hand/finger contact, wrist range, elbow/shoulder/trunk support, first fault, actual exposure, symptoms, downstream wrist demand, and escalation without diagnosis.
USA Gymnastics separately lists palms-on-floor forward rocking and backs-of-hands backward rocking, supporting distinct wrist-extension and wrist-flexion tasks.

Keep palms-down, changed finger direction, circular, unilateral, palm-lift, isometric, tall-plank, raised-support, banded, manual, and assessment tasks outside the exact Source 31 variant until separately authored and reviewed.

alternateAssessments.name: Rear-Facing Palms-Up Wrist Rock, Back-of-Hand Wrist Rock, or Wrist-Flexion Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: These aliases fit only when bilateral dorsal-hand contact, palms up, fingers toward the knees, and the exact backward-and-forward cycle are stated.

alternateAssessments.name: Smaller Backward Range
alternateAssessments.rationale: Comfortable backward range changes dose while contacts, hand orientation, action, and return remain exact.

alternateAssessments.name: Tempo or Brief Comfortable Endpoint Pause
alternateAssessments.rationale: Controlled pace and a short non-forced pause change exposure rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Repetitions, Sets, or Rest
alternateAssessments.rationale: Volume and recovery change dose rather than the task.

alternateAssessments.name: Stable Knee Cushioning
alternateAssessments.rationale: A stable pad under the knees changes contact comfort without changing the dorsal-hand surface or action.

alternateAssessments.name: Thin Firm Dorsal-Hand Comfort Pad
alternateAssessments.rationale: Padding under the hands changes pressure distribution, friction, cleanliness, and support interface and requires explicit validation.

alternateAssessments.name: Side-Facing Palms-Up Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Changing finger direction changes forearm rotation, wrist line, pressure, and available range.

alternateAssessments.name: Unilateral Back-of-Hand Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: One-hand emphasis changes laterality, load distribution, trunk demand, and failure consequences.

alternateAssessments.name: Raised-Support Back-of-Hand Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: A wall, bench, box, or other raised surface changes equipment, support height, load, angles, station, and failure consequences.

alternateAssessments.name: Seated or Non-Quadruped Back-of-Hand Wrist Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Removing the hands-and-knees base changes support, bodyweight transfer, floor access, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Rockers — Palms Down
alternateAssessments.rationale: Palmar hand support with fingers forward and wrist-extension loading changes the contact surface, joint action, loading direction, and endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Finger Pulses / Palm Lifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Active palm-heel lifting and finger/knuckle pressure are distinct hand actions rather than dorsal-hand bodyweight rocking.

alternateAssessments.name: Wrist Lean Isometric / Wrist Support Rock Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A sustained isometric endpoint or tall-plank support changes count, duration, leverage, load, purpose, and fatigue.

alternateAssessments.name: Quadruped Wrist Pronation-Supination Shifts
alternateAssessments.rationale: Changing hand orientation during loading adds forearm rotation and multiple directional wrist exposures.

alternateAssessments.name: Back-of-Hand Wrist Circles
alternateAssessments.rationale: Circular pressure travel adds lateral checkpoints, direction counting, and different dorsal-hand exposure.

alternateAssessments.name: Tall-Plank Back-of-Hand Rock or Planche Lean
alternateAssessments.rationale: Toe support and long leverage materially increase wrist, shoulder, trunk, and fatigue demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Banded Wrist-Flexion Mobilization
alternateAssessments.rationale: An anchored band changes joint force direction, equipment, setup, contraindications, and scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Fist or Parallette Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: Neutral-wrist gripping support removes the exact dorsal-hand wrist-flexion interface.

alternateAssessments.name: Loaded or Partner-Resisted Back-of-Hand Rock
alternateAssessments.rationale: External load or manual force changes magnitude, consent, equipment, failure risk, and coaching scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Clinical Wrist-Flexion Range or Pain Assessment
alternateAssessments.rationale: A measured assessment adds examiner protocol, clinical purpose, outcomes, consent, and different stop/escalation rules.
